label: late original-phase / delimiter steps of long sequences starting with a labial-ish letter (p,b,r,l,g)
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (139 activations in 1M sequences, weak magnitudes ~0.1-0.19). Fires only at the last ~3 original-phase steps (t=5..8) or the <DEL> step, almost always in L=9 sequences (84% of mass, rate peaks at t=8, the final original token). Never fires in the copy phase or at t<5. The sequence context is strongly skewed: first token is p/b/r/l/g (p alone ~35% of mass), p usually appears among the first few tokens (often orig(1)=p), and z/v/x tend to appear in the middle; the current input is often n/c/b/a or <DEL>. The predicate (late original/delimiter step, first token in {p,b,r,l,g}) captures ~90% of activations and mass but precision is ~0.05%: the feature fires on only a tiny, unidentified subset of matching contexts; adding conditions (seen p, seen z/v/x, current token in a/b/c/n, L=9) raises precision only to <1% while losing recall. Looks like a rare conjunction of hidden-state history rather than a clean token-level concept.
